newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico's Radio Centro to seek capital for telecoms.
newsitem.headline: Mexico's Radio Centro to seek capital for telecoms.

text.p: Mexican radio group Grupo Radio Centro SA said Tuesday it planned to seek $56 million of outside capital during the third quarter of this year for its new telephone venture Amaritel.

Radio Centro president Adrian Aguirre told a news conference that while his group wanted to maintain operating control over the venture -- it currently holds 51 percent of the capital -- it wanted fresh partners to put up money.
Aguirre admitted that the project had been delayed and had suffered problems but said he believed Radio Centro now had a viable business plan for Amaritel.

The telecomms venture had a license for long distance telephone service but this would not be Amaritel's main interest, he added. The company would instead focus on local telephone service and value-added products with a strong emphasis on quality service.

Aguirre said the share structure of Telmex -- where Carlos Slim is in the drivers seat with less than 20 percent of the equity -- could provide an example for Amaritel, where Radio Centro's stake would be diluted by fresh capital but control would be kept.
At present Radio Centro's minority partner with 49 percent of the equity is U.S. Global Telecommunications Inc, a subsididary of U.S. Telecom Holdings Inc.
Radio Centro has so far supplied around $7.14 million of capital for Amaritel and Aguirre said the company hoped it could limit any future exposure to needs financeable from working capital only.

Radio Centro wanted Amaritel to operate as a wholly separate project which involved no financial risk for the group, he added. The government concession requires Amaritel to start offering service by February 1998.
